title: Driving in the darkness
caption: Orion above the road to Cerro Paranal, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at Paranal Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: A curved road winds up a dark mountainside toward the summit of Cerro Paranal, home of ESO's Very Large Telescope. In the centre of the image, the constellation Orion stands out clearly in the night sky.
Driving this road after dark is a real challenge. It climbs from the Residencia Hotel to the summit, and once the Sun has set, cars are not allowed to use any lights except their parking lights.

The caption does not spell out the reason, but observatories in general go to great lengths to protect the darkness. Headlights sweeping across the mountain would spill stray light toward the telescopes, which are built to collect the faintest possible glow from distant objects. At an observatory, even a little artificial light can get in the way of the science.

understand.summary: This is a landscape photograph taken in visible light with a camera near Paranal. The camera settings and colour processing are not published.
understand.eye: Orion's bright stars are easy to see with the naked eye, but a long exposure reveals many fainter stars around the constellation.

explore: The road links two parts of the site: the Residencia Hotel below and the telescopes on the summit above, where the night's observations take place. Orion shines in the centre of the view.
alt: A dark, curving mountain road under a starry sky with the constellation Orion in the centre.
